handoff.purpose: Define FanoutTask, FanoutResult, and the per-call provider invocation with flight-recorder metadata.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY
symbols.note: Concurrency ceiling, 8, with measured rationale.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S
symbols.note: Per-call timeout ceiling, 300 seconds.

symbols.name: default_concurrency
symbols.note: Reads DAEDALUS_FANOUT_CONCURRENCY; returns max(1, int) or DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY on missing/invalid.

symbols.name: FanoutTask
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass: task_id, objective, paths, votes, meta; key property derives safe filename.

symbols.name: FanoutTask.key
symbols.note: Sanitizes task_id, collapses dot runs, truncates to 80, appends SHA-256 digest prefix.

symbols.name: FanoutResult
symbols.note: Dataclass: task_id, key, votes_requested, answers, errors, meta, resumed, trace_id; ok and blocked properties; to_dict.

symbols.name: FanoutResult.ok
symbols.note: True iff answers is non-empty.

symbols.name: FanoutResult.blocked
symbols.note: True iff every answer has report.status == 'blocked'.

symbols.name: FanoutResult.to_dict
symbols.note: Serializes result fields, including votes_collected.

symbols.name: _one_call
symbols.note: Imports DeepSeekProvider locally, builds objective with brief, runs provider, returns vote dict with sent digest metadata.

claims.text: The guard is not optional here and not a parameter -- a fan-out is exactly the shape that turns a missing guard into a bill.
claims.why: No install_process_guard call or guard reference appears in this chunk; the guard installation must occur elsewhere (likely fan_out in the next chunk).

claims.text: fan_out now REFUSES the combination [of votes>1 with temperature==0].
claims.why: No refusal logic is present in this chunk; fan_out is not defined here.

claims.text: Sharing an instance across worker threads would reintroduce that race by another door, so each call gets its own.
claims.where: module docstring (A FRESH PROVIDER PER CALL)
claims.why: _one_call constructs DeepSeekProvider() on line 114, once per call.

claims.text: Tasks that name paths get daedalus.lanes.graph_brief.render_brief prepended.
claims.where: module docstring (THE GRAPH GOES IN THE PROMPT)
claims.why: render_brief is imported, but the actual prepending logic (where brief is built and passed to _one_call) is not in this chunk; _one_call only receives brief as a parameter.

claims.text: RESULTS ARE PUBLISHED, NOT WRITTEN. Via daedalus.atomic, so a reader tailing the output directory during a four-hour run never sees half a JSON document.
claims.where: module docstring (RESULTS ARE PUBLISHED, NOT WRITTEN)
claims.why: write_text_atomic is imported, but no write call appears in this chunk; the write must happen in fan_out/resume logic elsewhere.

claims.text: Advisory only. There is no writable parameter and adding one would be a mistake.
claims.why: _one_call passes writable=False explicitly on line 125; no writable parameter exists in FanoutTask or _one_call.

claims.text: Concurrency from the environment, or DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY.
claims.why: Function returns DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY when env var missing or invalid, else max(1, int(raw)).

claims.text: It is derived from task_id rather than trusted, because a task id built from a commit message or a file path will contain separators.
claims.why: key property computes safe from task_id and appends digest; no separate trusted key field.

claims.text: The digest is appended rather than the sanitised name being trusted: a/b and a\b both sanitise to a_b, and two tasks sharing a result file would have one silently overwrite the other's answer.
claims.why: The code appends a SHA-256 digest of the raw task_id, so distinct inputs with same sanitized name get different keys.

claims.text: Dot runs are collapsed after sanitising. Replacing separators already makes traversal impossible, but ../../etc/passwd still produced .._.._etc_passwd -- a key that cannot escape and reads as though it were trying to.
claims.why: Sanitization replaces separators with underscores, then while '..' in safe replaces with '_', then lstrip('._'). For '../../etc/passwd' → '.._.._etc_passwd' → '_.._etc_passwd' → '__etc_passwd' → 'etc_passwd' after lstrip, so no leading dots remain.

claims.text: A name that looks like an attack invites someone to 'harden' it later by a route that breaks resume.
claims.why: This is a design rationale not directly checkable in code; the sanitization behavior is checked above.

claims.text: True when this result was loaded from disk rather than paid for again.
claims.why: The field exists with default False, but no loading logic is in this chunk.

claims.text: From daedalus.spine.envelope.current_trace_id, which NEVER mints -- so None means 'no trace was in scope', not 'here is a fresh unrelated id'.
claims.why: current_trace_id is imported, but not called in this chunk; its behavior is external.

claims.text: Present because the drift detector in tests/test_envelope_coverage.py caught this module as an undeclared record producer on 2026-07-30 and it was right: these files record a PAID external call and its answer, so a trace id correlates a bill to the run that incurred it.
claims.why: Historical justification; no test or trace assignment in this chunk.

claims.text: ok answers 'did the transport produce answers'; this answers 'did any of them carry evidence'.
claims.why: blocked returns True only if answers is non-empty and all answers have report.status == 'blocked'; ok is just bool(answers).

claims.text: A unit with at least one non-blocked answer stays un-blocked, because partial evidence is evidence.
claims.why: The all() over answers means any non-blocked answer makes blocked False.

claims.text: policy is handed to the provider, which passes it to daedalus.sensitivity.classify_data. Default None means the project's own policy applies.
claims.why: policy is passed to provider.run, but the provider's behavior is external to this chunk.

claims.text: It cannot lift the secret floor. providers/deepseek.py calls secret_floor_rule per path independently of classify_data... Verified with a fully permissive policy: source files pass, .env is still refused.
claims.why: secret_floor_rule and provider internals are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Imported here, not at module scope: this module is imported by tooling that must not pull the provider stack (and its network config) just to read the dataclasses.
claims.why: The import of DeepSeekProvider is inside the function, not at module top.

claims.text: BEFORE the question, not after. A model that has already read the question treats the brief as supporting material; a model that reads the brief first treats the question as being about the thing described.
claims.why: The code prepends brief to objective before the task text, constructing objective as brief + instructions + original objective.

claims.text: The brief above is DERIVED STRUCTURE...
claims.why: The string is exactly as quoted, prepended before the task.

claims.text: fresh per call -- see module docstring
claims.why: DeepSeekProvider() is instantiated on line 114 inside the function.

claims.text: operator-set egress scope, or None
claims.why: policy parameter is passed through to provider.run.

claims.text: lane-specific prompt, or None
claims.why: system_override parameter is passed through to provider.run.

claims.text: >0 is what makes votes independent
claims.why: The enforcement that temperature>0 when votes>1 is not in this chunk; only the parameter pass-through.

claims.text: advisory only, structurally
claims.why: writable=False is hardcoded on line 125.

claims.text: DIGESTS, NOT BODIES, for the prompt: the objective carries whole file contents, and a recorder that copies them turns a 4 KB result file into a 60 KB one and duplicates the repo across runs/.
claims.why: The sent dict stores objective_sha256 and objective_chars, not the objective body.

claims.text: The system message IS kept whole: it is small, shared, and it was the thing nobody could see.
claims.why: The code stores system_override_sha256 and system_override_chars, not a whole system message. The comment claims the system message is kept whole, but the code only keeps a digest of system_override; the actual system message may be internal to the provider and not recorded here.

claims.text: The digest is what answers the questions that matter -- 'did these three votes see the same prompt', 'did the prompt change between runs', 'is this result stale' -- and those are identity questions, which is exactly what a hash is for.
claims.why: The code records objective_sha256 and system_override_sha256, enabling such comparisons.

observations.what: _one_call constructs DeepSeekProvider() with no arguments, but the provider may require configuration from environment or defaults; this is uncheckable here.

The flight recorder comment claims 'The system message IS kept whole' but the code only stores a hash and char count of system_override; the actual system message may be internal to provider.run and not recorded, making the claim misleading in context.

temperature is passed through with a default of 0.0; the module docstring says fan_out refuses votes>1 with temperature 0, but that refusal is not in this chunk. If fan_out in the next chunk does not enforce it, the docstring would be broken.
The key property truncates to 80 characters before appending the digest, so the full key length is 91 characters; this is not a problem but worth noting for path length limits.

blocked property checks a['report'].get('status') == 'blocked' but does not validate that 'report' is a dict before calling .get; however, it does isinstance(a.get('report'), dict) in the same condition, so it is safe.

risks: _one_call line 114 | low | DeepSeekProvider() constructed with no explicit configuration; if provider requires constructor args or environment setup, calls may fail at runtime. | Check provider constructor signature in daedalus/providers/deepseek.py.

_one_call sent dict | medium | Comment claims system message is kept whole, but code only stores digest; if downstream debugging relies on the full system message, it is absent. | Verify whether provider.run returns the system message or if it is internal; if not, the recorder should include it.

_one_call signature | high | temperature defaults to 0.0 and votes can be >1 in FanoutTask; if fan_out (next chunk) does not enforce temperature>0 when votes>1, the module docstring's refusal claim is broken and fake agreement is possible. | Inspect fan_out in next chunk for a guard that raises when votes>1 and temperature==0.

FanoutTask.key | low | Key length is 91 characters (80 + '-' + 10), which may exceed filesystem limits on some systems (rare). | Confirm the target filesystem supports 91-char filenames; if not, adjust truncation length.

FanoutResult.blocked | low | The condition is safe but relies on the provider's report shape; if report.status is not exactly 'blocked' for refusals, the property may misclassify. | Check provider's report schema for refusal status values.
